The Department’s regulations provide that the E&S plan shall be present at the project site during all stages of an earth disturbance activity. Site appears to have been recently re-graded. Department recommends Operator temporarily stabilize site in order to prevent any potential pollution events from occurring. Violations are being issued for failure to have an E&S plan on-site for all stages of an earth disturbance activity and for failure to design, implement, and maintain E&S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.

Comments: On May 20 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the CFR USX 5 OG Well in regards to violations issued under inspection report 4157445.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department again observed the water flowing onto the access road. It did not appear any remedial actions have been taken to address the flowing water and resulting erosion and sedimentation issues on the access road.The water was observed flowing down the access road where it appeared to end at the well site. Erosion channels appear to have formed along the access road as a result of the flowing water. The water appears to be originating from a drainage channel/tributary to Antram Run. It appears that a culvert located under the access road may be damaged or obstructed, causing the water to flow onto the access road rather than through the culvert. The Department was unable to locate/inspect the culvert inlet. However, no water was observed discharging from the culvert outlet.These observations are consistent with observations from the Department's previous inspections (IR 4157445 and 4178222)Upon inspection of the well posting, it appeared to contain the well permit number, operator's name, and operator's phone number. However, it did not appear to contain the operator's address. The Department recommends the operator ensure all required information is properly posted in accordance with OGA3211(G).Based on today's inspection, violations issued in IR 4157445 remain outstanding.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2016-06-13 to Swn Production Co Llc in Bridgewater Twp, Susquehanna county. 78.56(a) - PITS AND TANKS FOR TEMPORARY CONTAINMENT - Operator failed to contain pollutional substances and wastes from the drilling, altering, completing, recompleting, servicing and plugging the well, including brines, drill cuttings, drilling muds, oils, stimulation fluids, well treatment and servicing fluids, plugging and drilling fluids other than gases in a pit, tank or series of pits and tanks.

Violation ID 761582

Unconventional Y
County Susquehanna

Inspection Type Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date 2016-06-13
Comments Inspection of the Range 84 Markovitch Well Pad in response to a spill report by the operator. The incident occurred on Friday, June 10, 2016 at approximately 8:30 p.m. Initially, the spill was reported to Southwestern Energy (SWN) by the carrier as less than 5-gallons and clean-up began. A visual inspection by SWN personnel on the morning of Saturday, June 11th revealed the spill may have been more than initially thought and the spill was reported to DEP NERO's Emergency Response at 9:00 a.m. The information reached the Scranton O&G office at 9:00 a.m. on June 13, 2016. I spoke to SWN's Afton Sterling via telephone while on-site to obtain the details of the spill. I also received follow-up emails from SWN’s Mike Deming that relayed some other details of the incident. A summary of both sources indicates that a waste water truck was in the process of loading production water from the production tank on the pad when the production fluid foamed in the truck and spilled over. The process was halted and clean up began with absorbent material and shovels. Due to the darkness and the foamy nature of the release, the quantity was initially difficult to estimate. On the morning of the 11th, the spill was reported DEP as approximately 10-gallons. The spill occurred directly in front of the production tank containment area where the truck connection is and affected the soil/gravel of the pad surface. The spill was not on containment. An area approximately 14-feet x 10-feet and 5-inches deep was excavated, yielding approximately 2-3 cubic yards of soil/gravel. The excavation base and perimeter was screened in 26 locations using a conductivity meter with results of less than 100 micro Siemens. Due to the volume of soil, and size of the excavation, the actual amount of fluid spilled was likely less than what was reported to DEP. The excavated soil was loaded onto a small dump truck for transport to the Meshoppen Rail Yard for ultimate disposal at the Tunnel Hill Reclamation Facility in New Lexington, Ohio. Work was completed and there was no one other than myself on-site at the time of the inspection. I observed an area approximately the size described that had been excavated and fresh gravel/soil had been replaced. There were no other indications of contamination on the ground. "Violations Immediately Corrected" were documented for contamination impacting the ground surface as follows: 58 P.S. § 3218.2; Containment for unconventional wells. 35 P.S. §6018.301; Management of residual waste. 25 Pa. code § 78.56(a); Pits and tanks for temporary containment. 35 P.S. § 691.402(b) Potential Pollution.

A section of open soils was displaying rills leading into the channel. Gravel was noted above the inlet, flowing over towards the channel. Remnants of gravel/sediment noted leading off the beginning of the access road towards the main township road (Photo 25).The violations issued on 03/11/2024 remain outstanding. A violation of 102.22(b)1 is being issued for the lack of temporary stabilization and the associated accelerated erosion.

Violation ID: 927037
Permit API: 053-30017
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Harmony Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/18/2021
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to Pennfield Energy's 8/17/2021 notification of a crude oil discharge from a stock tank located at the Milford South tank battery, which is located adjacent to this well site. Per Matt Duckett (field representative for Pennfield Energy) the oil/water separator that serves this tank battery failed and resulted in all production fluids entering the stock tank, which did not have the capacity to hold all of the fluid. Crude oil then discharged from an open vent on top of one of the stock tanks and onto the ground within an earthen containment that surrounds all of the tanks at the Milford South tank battery. The estimated quantity of crude oil that was released has been revised after conducting remediation work. Matt Duckett stated that approximately five barrels of crude is a more accurate quantity of product actually released as a result of this incident. Additional details regarding the release can be found in the 'Remarks/Violations' section of this report. This well is equipped for production with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the jack's electric box.

It appeared a landowner stream crossing on the southwest side of the pad outside the constructed LOD had a new culvert and stone installed. Violation ID: 8215508

Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/29/2025
Comments: On January 29, 2025, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection at the EQT ARO LLC H Lyle Landon Well Pad A. This inspection is a follow up to EQT reporting a spill on January 24, 2025, where a dump to one of the production fluid tanks failed. Upon failing, the pressure caused production fluid to mist outside of containment onto the well pad surface. According to EQT, it was thought that the majority of the production fluid was released into the production fluid containment. DEP placed a phone call to Rick Hall with EQT at 0848 on January 29, 2025 to gather more information on the spill. Mr. Hall informed DEP that during EQT's investigation of the spill that more than a mist event had occurred. While the majority of the produced fluid spilled into containment, an area of high soil conductivity was found outside of containment to the south next to the containment wall. EQT suspects there is an area of the liner for the containment that is leaking. Since January 24, 2025, EQT has vacuumed all the fluid out of the containment and power washed the containment liner. Mr. Hall said there were no visible or apparent holes found. The impacted soil that could be removed has been excavated. EQT plans to remove the production fluid tanks and the containment to investigate and remove the remainder of the impacted soil underneath the containment. A schedule for this process has not yet been made. EQT plans to monitor the area and remove impacted soil or production fluid as needed until the area can be completely remediated. On January 24, 2025, Penn E and R was onsite to collect waste classification samples and oversee the excavation. EQT plans to go through the Act 2 remediation process due to the unknown volume of fluid that leaked through the containment.Due to the spill of production fluid outside of containment violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted.

The contractors are setting up defensive measures to prevent oil from entering a pond that is fed by the watercourse. The pond is located approximately 50 feet past the last visible oil. The crude oil pushed to the surface at the Hart 3 well and there is oil that has traveled over the ground near the well. Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 845145
Permit API: 113-20411
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Cherry Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-03-27
Comments: I received at call at 07:30 from Eric Hottenstein of Chesapeake to inform the Department of a release of oil-based drilling mud. He then told me that he would also call the main number to report the spill. I arrived onsite at 09:25 and met with Eric Hottenstein and Nick Krut, both of Chesapeake. We went to observe the release and they described what had occurred. Some newer wells on the pad were recently stimulated and were being set up for flowback. These wells had the intermediate annulus plumbed to a sentry valve (Photo #1). The valves are designed to vent to prevent a build up of pressure. It is believed that the mechanism inside this valve may have become stuck and allowed a build up of pressure causing the top of the valve to come off and release oil-based drilling mud. The area around the wells was partially covered by secondary containment. A section had been removed around the older wells on the site in order to perform maintenance. The unprotected area consisted of both the gravel pad surface and the cement apron around the older wells (Photos #3 & 6). The released drilling mud coated parts of the 105H well, secondary containment, gravel pad, older wells, and cement apron. Eric and Nick believed that a total of 42 gallons of drilling mud was released with 21 gallons on containment and 21 gallons off containment. Before I arrived Mountain Energy was already onsite and had used a Super Sucker to remove the free portion of the drilling mud. They were in the process of power washing the apron and allowing the water/mud mixture to drain into the well cellars (Photo #7). The well heads were going to be washed next with water and degreaser. The well cellars are cement lined and should be sealed to allow the collected water to be vacuumed out. The gravel portion was going to be scraped and excavated as needed. Chesapeake also mentioned pulling back some of the remaining secondary containment to remove and mud that may have seeped underneath. The 105H annulus was connected to a day tank (approx. 350 gallon poly tank) that was in secondary containment. This was a precautionary measure in the event of a second release. Crews were also onsite installing flowback equipment and checking the annulus pressure gauges to monitor the situation. Eric believed the area would be cleaned in about 2 hours. He also mentioned that the day tanks may be installed on other wells in the future to prevent another release. Violations noted.

Violation ID: 8182294
Permit API: 125-22817
Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 4/04/2024
Comments: On 04/04/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 Well Site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). On 03/11/2024, the violations were issued as outstanding (IR 3726997). The operator was in compliance with schedule on 03/27/2024 (IR 3736262).The following was observed during inspection on 04/04/2024:Inspection conducted after several large rain events. The beginning upper part of the channel was displaying accelerated erosion and rills entering the channel (Photos 1, 2). The opposite side of the road was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Sediment accumulation was noted within the stabilized area with establishing vegetation (Photos 3, 4). Upper culvert inlet was blocked with sediment (Photo 5).Several sections of the bank above the channel did not have temporary stabilization. A section of open soils was displaying rills leading into the channel. The channel was also displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation (Photos 6, 7).The middle culvert was completely blocked with sediment. Gravel was noted above the inlet, flowing over towards the channel. Debris and channelization were noted leaving the culvert inlet (Photos 8-10).The outlet of the middle culvert had sediment accumulation within the grass and accelerated erosion below (Photos 11-15).Outlet of roadside channel was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. It was noted that sediment and flow were also both coming from the direction of the Landowner's building, in addition to the site's channel. Sediment accumulation within vegetation leading to the collection box and the site's middle culvert (Photos 16-20).Sediment accumulation within culvert and the outlet. This leads towards the stream (Photos 21, 22).Several rills leading off site and towards the roadside channel near the beginning section of the access road (Photos 23, 24). Remnants of gravel/sediment noted leading off the beginning of the access road towards the main township road (Photo 25).The violations issued on 03/11/2024 remain outstanding. A violation of 102.22(b)1 is being issued for the lack of temporary stabilization and the associated accelerated erosion.

No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the gas wellhead. At the time of this inspection, the Department attempted to contact the Operator by calling the number posted on the well tag, however, the number was not in service, therefore violations are being issued at this time for failure to have updated and accurate information posted on the well posting.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a small production tank adjacent to the gas wellhead, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this tank. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site. The tank on the left was observed to be green and the tank on the right was observed to be a faded green color. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the green (left) production tank on site, however, the faded green (right) production tank was observed to have several corroded pipes connected to it. Towards the top of the faded green (right) production tank, the Department observed an area where severe corrosion caused piping to break off. This broken pipe was observed to be on the ground at the base of the production tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this broken pipe, from the other corroded pipes still connected to the production tank, or the production tank at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the area at the base of the faded green production tank under/adjacent to the corroded pipes. Although, these soil conductivity readings (0.0328 mS, 0.0899 mS, and 0.0244 mS) are not elevated, it does not visual appear that the release that previously occurred has yet to be remediated as vegetation in this area appears to be distressed and the gravel in this area is stained. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed production equipment connected to a meter box, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment or meter box. Inside the Meter Box, the Department observed production paper that was dated 10/27/2023. A pile of pipes was observed on the ground adjacent to the meter box and production equipment, the Department recommends any equipment not in use be removed from the well site. Violations are being issued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not in use from the gas well site. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from corroded and broken piping is to remain outstanding at this time and new violations are being issued at this time for inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8277571
Permit API: 123-47192
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/08/2026
Comments: Evidence of stressed and dead vegetation in the vicinity of the Akins lease tank battery was visible from Rounds Hill Road. Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) and I (Mat Haemer WQS-DEP) were present for this inspection. This inspection was conducted to document findings of an apparent release of production fluids from the Akins tank battery, as well as a separate release from a brine tank previously removed from the nearby Loomis lease's tank battery. Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners previously indicated that he had checked and found the integrity of the Loomis lease brine tank to be sufficient for future use. Kyle indicated that the tank was empty and would be unused until repurposed.The PVC drain line within the secondary containment area of the Akins tank battery was found to be improperly placed. The PVC line straddles the cutout hole in the surface of the brine tank in such a manner that fluids draining through the line would be able to flow over the surface of the brine tank and pool within the secondary containment area. Soil within secondary containment immediately below the PVC line was found to have specific conductance in excess of 17,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. Evidence of pooling was visible in the containment area via crude oil staining and stressed vegetation. This indicates that fluid once filled the secondary containment, but apparently was able to migrate downward and/or outward through the secondary containment diking. Stressed and dead vegetation downslope and immediately outside the secondary containment dike further indicates the likelihood that the integrity of the secondary containment is inadequate. Understory vegetation was killed in an area approximately 30 feet wide by 200 feet long. Soils in the killzone were found to have elevated specific conductivity in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.The brine tank staged on location was found to have evidence of stressed and dead vegetation beginning from a point immediately beneath the drain valve and continuing downslope beyond the tank in an area approximately 10 feet wide by 200 feet in length. Specific conductivity in soils below the drain valve measured in excess of 8,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. Soils in the killzone downslope of the brine tank were found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with brine disposal receipts for the Akins lease. The Akins Lease Akins 1 OG Well was found to have an illegible ID tag.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8211458
Permit API: 047-24792
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/17/2024
Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone called made by Jeff Passarello, of Seneca Resources, to Brian Ayers, WQS Supervisor with the Department, on December 16, 2024. The purpose of the phone call was to report an incident which had occurred on Clermont Pad D. It was reported that approximately a total of 10 barrels of production fluid was released from a pipeline while doing maintenance on a pump. The pump was in secondary containment at the time of the incident. The system which controlled the flow of production fluid had not been turned off before performing maintenance on the pump. As a result, production fluid projected out of the pipeline. It is estimated that approximately 5 barrels of production fluid remained in secondary containment and approximately 5 barrels of production fluid discharged onto the well pad outside of the secondary containment. Upon arrival to the site, it was noted that the pump had been removed and placed on the pad away from where the spill occurred. The system controlling the flow of production fluid had been turned off, resolving the source of where the spill had originated. An excavator was used to remove contaminated material from the well pad. Four dumpsters were on site which contained the contaminated waste from the incident. The released production fluid appeared to be primarily within 10 yards of where the incident occurred and remained on the pad. There was no evidence of any production fluid off the well site.Confirmatory field sampling will occur to confirm full remediation of the site. Follow up inspections will be performed routinely until the cleanup is deemed complete.

Comments: This site located west off Greeley Road north of junction with Francis Road in a forested area. Tank battery, two brine tanks and one oil tank in secondary containment, located along the access road. Marshall Wurst found this tank battery with a lined secondary containment containing a release of 2-3 bbls of crude oil on 8/23/2019. WQS Taylor inspected this site on 8/28/2019 and issued an NOV to Coastal Petro Corp. for the release of crude oil into the lined secondary containment. There was 1 1/2'-2' of crude oil/water in the secondary containment at the time of initial inspection. There is ice and snow covering most of the bottom of the secondary containment making it unclear as to the extent of the clean-up however the ice around the tanks appears to be clear and does not contain any residual oil contamination. An empty plastic 200 gallon is set in the secondary containment between the oil tank and first brine tank. A follow-up inspection will be completed when there is a thaw and the stone in the secondary containment can be inspected for contamination. This well to be transferred from Coastal Petro Corp. to Titusville Oil & Gas Associates Inc., application for the transfer of wells was sent in on 11/18/2019. Titusville Oil & Gas Associates, Inc. is to complete the clean-up at this site.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation ID: 986498
Permit API: 015-23717
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Twp
Inspection Type: Drilling/Alteration
Inspection Date: 3/01/2023
Comments: On 3/1/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Floydie well site. It was 44 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. Snowfall had impacted the region within the last 48 hours. Water puddles were scattered across the pad surface. Fracking operations have ceased and most of the frac equipment along with the site secondary containment have been removed from the site. There still are six frac tanks in place along the east side of location. These were not staged in secondary containment and were not connected to any equipment at the time of the inspection. Crews were working at installing the production pipe and equipment on the ten wells. No wells were in production at the time of the inspection. Well permit numbers were posted at the entrance to the access road. I did witness a steady stream of bubbles coming up from beside the casing on the 122HC well. I passed the issue with the bubbling along to Rich Herbstritt for follow-up.I field tested many of the water puddles that were scattered around location with the following results: A 100' x 12' strip of water along the perimeter berm along the northeast edge of the pad field tested at as high as 3.485 mS conductance. Other readings were 2.6, 2.3, 1.5, and 1.3 mS. The water was 0.9 mS where the flow was leaving through the perimeter berm opening, running down into infiltration berm A1.A 30' x 40' water puddle on the south east side of location near two frac tanks field tested at 9.05 mS conductance.A 30' by 30' water/mud area on the south east side of location field test at as high as 12.61 mS conductance.A 100' x 100' water/muddy area east of the wellheads field tested at 8.30 mS conductance on the southern side tapering off to 5.0 mS conductance on the north side of the water/mud area.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by six infiltration berms that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID #3492400 for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface during completion operations with an unknown volume impacting the unprotected pad surface. The DEP recommends the following:1. Assess the integrity of the 122HC well and repair as necessary2. Continue with Act 2 remediation for areas with suspectedcontamination.I left the site at 1400 hours.
